blocking_question: (1) the merged trait+interface dispatch default has no consumer (same trigger as mlir); (2) eager construction-time verification (xDSL) vs deferred checkpoint verification (MLIR) is an explicit fork for whoever designs ASIR verification

measurement.fork_1: settled by G89: neither precondition of an external-model registry holds in Atlas (a Rust trait impl attaches capabilities statically; no code loads at runtime; ACP attach_capability is data), so the merged model is ordinary Rust traits, with no registry and no TypeId map
measurement.fork_2: settled by ASIR-CONSTRUCTION-MODEL.md (CONTRACT): an ACP transaction is a batch verified as an isolated post-transaction candidate through schema, type, semantic, architectural, security and obligation validation before 'apply transaction', and the graph is verified again at 'verify + normalize + canonicalize + seal'. Value-level checks (xDSL's attribute __post_init__ verify) are the schema/type stages, run eagerly per payload; structural checks (MLIR's OperationVerifier) run at the transaction checkpoint. States inside a transaction are never observable, so neither pure form is needed
measurement.asir_state: ASIR is CONTRACT/TARGET; no op/attribute Rust types exist

decision.design_references_retained: the census's ADAPT dispositions and xdsl-merged-trait-interface-dispatch.md hold the design lessons for the TARGET ASIR; re-derive in Rust, never copy
